notes: GPT-6 Astra Pro; effort not exposed; reader_a; first reading. Original whole image was viewed once for layout and both native halves once, followed by twelve distinct saved crops. Existing crops were reused for final correction-span and punctuation assessment; no recrop, OCR, research or compilation.

Author page number 15 is in his hand. Lower folio 94 is thinner and lighter, attributed only to another unnamed archive-foliation hand. The proposed text uses margin for that folio; this is not a substantive witness-difference row.

The opening continues a preceding sentence, with plus visibly cancelled. The page records necessary conditions for an automorphism of the named groupoid to come from an element of Gamma: lifting to finite étale covers and invariance of kernels associated with maps defined over K, then a periodic-point variant.

The first margin says the two conditions depend on the operation on the fundamental group at one point. The NB complains about formulating the conditions from exterior actions; its live text lacks a secure copula. No deviennent or sont has been supplied.
The last sentence ends with a comma and continues beyond this page. Pense versus peux is left unresolved; no grammatical repair or missing verb is added.

The cancellation before the lower l’action de has separate low traces, but their reading as il y a remains low confidence because of overlap with the raised live phrase. The upper cancelled wording and cancelled Pi subscript are also unresolved.

The map target argument Y versus X and the mark above tilde Theta are unresolved independently. Both small based-group signs are capital Pi. Changing case is not treated as a mathematically consequential assertion by itself.
The first reader performed source reading and collation only, without a mathematical check. The separately identified root event below checks a conditional algebraic implication.

H italic extérieures and un are treated as representing the respective single source underlines; no macro-only difference row is counted. The second reading corrects the initial double-underline interpretation of un. The margin separator is preserved as a simple TikZ stroke.

The root review resolves the compact quantifier before hom. as ∀ from its pointed join, diagonal and crossbar; it is not expanded to a word. The first reader’s tt alternative remains documented in the raw report.

Root check 142-095-R1 verifies the formal kernel-invariance implication behind (b), conditional on commuting induced automorphisms: f*s=tf* makes ker f* stable, with equality because the automorphisms are invertible. The periodic-point wording requires the stated fixed-base-point power. This does not establish the proposed sufficient Galois criterion, and it does not decide the overinked target Y/X.

The complete second reading finds one separate straight underline below the connected bodies of un in the first marginal note. The main reader reused margin_first and agrees. Existing comparison row 095-37 is revised: C explicitly doubles the underline; H preserves the corresponding single emphasis.

Two tiny dark points directly below-left of the stable-sous Theta oval, approximately x847–854/y1794–1808, have no independent textual or annotative position. Auditor and main reader separately inspected them in star_map_lift and exclude them as incidental pen traces. No punctuation, drawing or inventory element is invented.

check_events.outcome: Conditional kernel-invariance step in condition (b): if f*:A→B is a group homomorphism and automorphisms s of A, t of B satisfy f* s=t f*, then s(ker f*)=ker f*. Forward inclusion follows from f*(s h)=t(1)=1; applying the same relation to inverse automorphisms gives the reverse inclusion. The argument also applies to a power when the relevant base point is fixed and the induced maps are defined. This verifies the formal naturality implication, not the existence of a compatible lift, the sufficient Galois criterion, or the unresolved target glyph.
